summary.intent: Manage the CipherBox v2.0 milestone via the GSD manager workflow: plan/execute/verify/ship phases 76, 78, 79, then triage backlog todos into closeout phases 80-83, discuss and implement Phase 80's rotation write-plane and recipient-pin durability work, debug the resulting e2e regressions on PR #615, and ultimately investigate a deep architectural question about grant delivery (relay-stored vs metadata-stored keys) that emerged from the debugging.
summary.outcome: Phases 76, 78, 79 shipped and merged (#610, #613, #611); closeout phases 80-83 were scoped from pending todos. Phase 80 was planned, executed, and shipped as PR #615, which required four rounds of debugging (desktop AES-GCM cascade, web upgrade pin-drop, file-rooted grant fail-closed, zeroization nit) before reaching merge-ready state with 0 unresolved threads. A follow-up request to fix the web file-grant re-mint gap uncovered two deeper bugs (base64/hex encoding mismatch, and file-leaf IPNS key unreachability in web's rotation walk) that led to pulling back the seam wiring and instead writing a formal research-goals document to guide an architecture decision between relay-stored and metadata-stored share grants.

repo: GSD background agents must `git checkout feat/<slug>` first in their isolation worktree since plans/artifacts live on the phase branch, not main — orchestrator re-homes to canonical `feat/<slug>` branches if a planner commits to an ephemeral `worktree-agent-*` branch instead.
`EnterWorktree` refuses repo-root→worktree switches; resumed/verify agents must use `git -C` or absolute-path scoped commands instead.
GSD commit helper can report `commit_failed` as a false negative even though the commit landed — verify with `git log` before retrying.

ship-phase.md pipeline: verify → secure → crypto/privacy review → validate → simplify → SDK-E2E gate → CodeRabbit → draft-PR-then-ready → resolve threads → extract learnings; SDK-E2E gate can't run twice concurrently (shared Postgres/Kubo state + :3000 bind), so parallel ships must serialize around it.

CodeRabbit `.coderabbit.yaml` has `drafts: false` (skips draft PRs); `pr-release-preview.yml` triggers on `opened` including drafts — so draft-first-then-ready avoids CodeRabbit reviewing a pre-release-bot-commit head.
Release targets in this repo are set via labels + a 'Release Preview' PR comment, not a `chore(release)` commit — absence of a bot commit on the branch is not a red flag.

`web-e2e`/`desktop-e2e` are workflow_dispatch-gated (not run on every PR push), so regressions in those suites only surface on manual dispatch or main-push — this is why Phase 78/80 regressions weren't caught by the standard ship pipeline.

`git commit` can appear to hang/timeout (~2min) due to the Entire post-commit hook or 1Password SSH signing after the commit object is already written — verify via `git log` before retrying, don't assume failure.

Entire CLI (git-hook-based session capture) does not capture Agent-tool subagent transcripts: they live in the harness task dir, not `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` which Entire watches; `--no-verify` commits (common in worktrees without deps) additionally skip the Entire hooks entirely. Upgrading Entire (0.7.7→0.8.42) does not add subagent capture.
Rebasing 40+ commits to resolve a bookkeeping-only conflict (ROADMAP.md/STATE.md) is the wrong tool — a single `git merge --no-edit main` resolves it once with far less churn.

recipient-pin enforcement (Phase 80, D-03e) is folder/root-only by design (D-03g carve-out) — file leaves have no `NodeWriteBody` and are structurally exempt from the fail-closed pin check across all consumers (Rust re-mint, TS re-mint, web upgrade/reconcile).

Desktop rotation (Rust/FUSE) re-mints grants inline via `node.kind`-aware `rotate_one`; web's `performScopeExitRotation` never wired the equivalent inline seam (`grantCallbacks: undefined`), relying instead on a separate `owner-reconcile` sweep that skips file roots at the folderTree gate — this asymmetry is the root of the file-grant re-mint gap.

sdk-core's `reMintGrantsRootedAt` emits the re-wrapped key as base64, but `PATCH /shares/:id/grant`'s `UpdateGrantDto.encryptedReadKey` requires hex — Rust's equivalent already emits hex (explicit code comment 'must be hex, NOT base64'); this silently broke ALL relay grant re-mints (folder and file) since no unit test exercises the real PATCH (only mocked).

v3 data model: `writeKey` (AES symmetric) is the shareable envelope that encrypts a node's write-body; `ipnsPrivateKey` (Ed25519 signing key, the actual publish authority) lives encrypted inside that write-body alongside the write-chain (`writeChildren`) — this indirection lets write access to a whole subtree be granted with a single ECIES wrap instead of O(nodes×writers).

Read rotation keeps `ipnsPrivateKey`/name/writeKey stable (rekeys only the read plane); write rotation mints a brand new `ipnsPrivateKey` → new IPNS name and tombstones the old — this is because a writer who already extracted the old signing key can only be excluded by changing the signing identity itself.

code.finding: reMintGrantsRootedAt encoded the re-wrapped grant key as base64 (bytesToBase64) but the PATCH /shares/:id/grant DTO requires hex — fixed to bytesToHex for cross-language parity with Rust.

rotateWriteFromNode's co-writer key re-wrap (encryptedWriteKey) is a probable sibling of the same base64/hex encoding bug on the write-plane rotation path — flagged as a todo, not fixed (out of read-rotation scope).

performScopeExitRotation calls rotateReadFromNode with innerGrants: undefined, grantCallbacks: undefined unconditionally — web never re-mints grants inline; all re-mint is delegated to the separate owner-reconcile sweep.

getRecipientPubkeyPins reader (folder-only, via requireFolder) plus a folderTree.get(ipns) gate at lines ~198-201/256-257 that skips file-rooted shares entirely — so file grants are re-minted by neither the inline path nor the sweep.

refresh_grant_root_recipient_pins added to fetch+unseal the grant root's currently-published write-body and overwrite the inode's cached recipient_pins before rotation reads them, fixing a real timing race where FUSE-T(macOS)/WinFsp(Windows) mounts read a stale empty pin cache before the ~30s periodic refresh, causing rotation to fail-closed.

resealAndPublishParent was rebuilding the parent write-body as {ipnsPrivateKey, writeChildren} only, silently dropping recipientPins on every shared-write republish — fixed to preserve parentNode.writeBody?.recipientPins verbatim.

workflow: Serialize SDK-E2E-gated ship pipelines rather than running them in parallel; run other stages (verify/plan/discuss) in parallel freely.

When a background agent's report makes a strong technical claim (e.g. 'test-only fix, not a product bug'), independently verify against the actual code before relaying it as fact to the user — caught the agent's own mis-framing of an AES-GCM bug as a seal/unseal AAD issue when it was actually a re-mint fail-closed cascade.

When re-verifying a PR reviewer's (greptile/CodeRabbit) persistent finding, always confirm you're checked out on the actual PR branch, not main — a wrong-branch read produced a false 'this code doesn't exist, finding is stale' conclusion that led to incorrectly resolving a real security thread.

Prefer polling CI/review state via the orchestrator's own backgrounded shell command (Bash run_in_background + Monitor-style polling) rather than re-invoking a subagent purely to wait — burns fewer tokens on poll loops.

When a background agent proposes a narrow patch to silence a reviewer finding but the fix wouldn't actually solve the underlying problem, refuse the cosmetic fix and either scope a real fix or document the gap as a tracked, deferred item with evidence.

For deep, contested architectural questions (relay-stored vs metadata-stored key material) that surface mid-implementation, stop coding and write a standalone research-goals document (with a concrete worked scenario as a shared benchmark) rather than deciding unilaterally or continuing to patch symptoms.

friction: Repeated wrong turns during Phase 80 debugging: initial hypothesis (AAD/seal-format bug) was wrong; a subsequent 'flake' framing of a CI failure had to be walked back after the user pointed to hard evidence; and a wrong-branch git checkout led to incorrectly resolving a real greptile security thread — required a formal correction and a feedback memory to be written.

Session/API quota limits interrupted background agents multiple times mid-execution (ship agent, execute agent, debug-fix agent), requiring resume-in-place logic each time to avoid losing partial commits.

Greptile re-reviews asynchronously after every push and re-raised the same finding three times with increasing specificity, requiring three separate rounds of investigation before the real gap was confirmed and properly fixed.
CodeRabbit rate-limiting delayed a full review pass by ~52 minutes mid-ship, requiring the team to push fixes ahead of the full review rather than block on it.

Cross-package TypeScript dist staleness (sdk-core/core built dist missing new fields like recipientPins) caused spurious typecheck errors that required a bottom-up rebuild (core → sdk-core → sdk) before real errors could be distinguished from stale-dist noise.

No local way to validate the desktop e2e pin-materialization fix (FUSE-T/WinFsp mounts) — had to rely entirely on CI dispatch-gated runs, adding multiple slow feedback-loop iterations (each ~10-15 min) to converge on a working fix.

Local reproduction of the sdk-e2e file-grant re-mint scenario required standing up a full Docker stack (postgres, kubo, redis, mock-ipns-routing, API) since no local harness previously wired rotationCallbacks — significant setup overhead for a single test.
open_items: PR #615 (Phase 80) and its associated research-goals doc work were left in-progress at session end — Gap C (base64→hex) fixed and committed, inline-seam wiring pulled back to a dormant/opt-in state, skipped e2e retained, research charter written; final commits (Gap C, web pullback, research doc) were being split and committed when the transcript ends.

recipient-pin-lifecycle-hardening todo (§5/§6) tracks: file shares have no substitution protection (D-03g), a stale-cache window where a routine folder mutation could drop a web-issued pin, and the confirmed-but-unfixed web file-grant re-mint gap (Gap B) requiring either engine-side write-chain key derivation or an architecture change.

Formal architecture decision deferred to a research/prototyping sprint: relay-stored vs metadata-stored share grant key material, hygiene-rekey vs revoking-rotation distinction, and the write-plane engine.ts:2833 base64/hex sibling bug — captured in .planning/research/grant-delivery-rotation-research-goals.md.

Recovery-tool large-file availability gap (dag-pb bodies >256KiB need trustless ?format=raw gateway API) flagged by the Phase 78 fix agent as a hardening todo, not yet formally logged as a separate pending todo file.
Phases 81 (TEE/IPNS correctness), 82 (wire-encoding hardening), and 83 (desktop resilience) remain undiscussed/unplanned as of session end.
PR #614 (ship-workflow draft-PR flow) and earlier PRs were merged by the user outside the assistant's visibility at times, requiring the assistant to sync/confirm state after the fact.
